topStories.headline: Mission Bay Elementary Opens Its Doors — SF's First New Public School in 20 Years
topStories.dek: The long-awaited Mission Bay School welcomed its first students on August 17, fulfilling a promise made to the neighborhood nearly three decades ago.
topStories.body:
Nearly 200 students filed into the brand-new Mission Bay School on Monday, August 17, marking a milestone that residents and city officials have anticipated since the neighborhood's 1998 redevelopment plan first set aside land for a public elementary campus. The school — the first new SFUSD building in approximately 20 years — serves pre-kindergarten through kindergarten in its inaugural 2026–27 year, with plans to expand one grade at a time until it reaches fifth grade and an enrollment of more than 400 students.

The $95 million, four-story building at 1415 Owens St., near the UCSF Medical Center, was constructed by McCarthy Building Company and funded in large part by San Francisco's 2016 school bond, Proposition A. Its design features wide, movable glass doors that blend classrooms and breakout spaces under a principle the school's architect, Chris McGiff-Brown, calls 'Universal Design for Learning.' A fourth-floor Mission Bay Learning Hub will draw high-school students from across the city into STEM career pathways.

SFUSD Superintendent Dr. Maria Su and Mayor Daniel Lurie attended the August 6 ribbon-cutting ceremony. Su referenced the longstanding commitment made when Mission Bay's redevelopment began. The neighborhood has nearly doubled in population over the last 15 years, driven by the UCSF campus, Chase Center, and a wave of new housing — yet families had continued to compete fiercely for seats at nearby Daniel Webster Elementary.

The new school shares the Daniel Webster attendance area, meaning all students in the zone — encompassing SoMa, Mission Bay, Potrero Hill, and Dogpatch — will receive the attendance-area tiebreaker at both campuses. SFUSD estimates Mission Bay Elementary will be fully enrolled by 2032. The district also noted that the opening comes as it grapples with roughly 14,000 empty seats citywide, a tension that city leaders acknowledged even as they celebrated the neighborhood's long-overdue school.

topStories.headline: $62 Million Gene Friend Recreation Center Reopens in SoMa After Two-Year Rebuild
topStories.dek: The newly reconstructed facility at 77 Harriet Street opened August 13 with two full-size basketball courts, a weight room, and expanded community space — more than doubling the footprint of the old gym.
topStories.body:
South of Market's only indoor public recreational facility threw open its doors on Thursday, August 13, after two years of demolition and construction that transformed a cramped 1990-era concrete bunker into a sleek, glass-walled community hub. The new Gene Friend Recreation Center, addressed at 77 Harriet Street (with the former project address at 270 Sixth Street), replaces a single-court gymnasium with a 25,000-square-foot facility featuring two full-length basketball courts flooded with natural light through expansive windows, a modern exercise area, a yoga studio, multipurpose rooms connected to a new exterior playground, and a kitchenette.

The $62 million project was financed through a mix of public and private sources, with the 2020 Health and Recovery Bond covering roughly half the cost. San Francisco Recreation and Park Department acquired a neighboring parcel at 240 Sixth Street for $7.1 million in 2024 to allow for potential future expansion. The center was designed by Mark Cavagnero Associates in collaboration with Kuth Ranieri Architects.

Rec and Park General Manager Sarah Madland and District 10 Supervisor Matt Dorsey spoke at the grand opening. Dorsey noted the neighborhood's rapid population growth in calling the facility 'our backyard.' The timing was deliberate: the center reopened just ahead of the first day of school for San Francisco Unified School District, providing after-school programming space for SoMa's children and teens who have had few public indoor options since the original facility closed in February 2024.

The Rec and Park Department also acquired an adjacent parcel at 240 Sixth Street, currently an auto repair shop under lease, which the city envisions as a long-term expansion site. No development timeline for that parcel has been announced.

topStories.headline: JPMorgan Commits $200M to Potrero Power Station, Accelerating Dogpatch Waterfront Redevelopment
topStories.dek: The nation's largest bank is financing 342 apartments on the Dogpatch waterfront and seeding a new fund for middle-income housing at the long-anticipated Power Station site.
topStories.body:
JPMorgan Chase announced early this month that it is committing nearly $200 million in financing to a 342-unit apartment project at the former Potrero Power Station on the Dogpatch waterfront, and separately staking up to $15 million in a new fund aimed at building middle-income housing in San Francisco. The move represents one of the largest single private investments in the Central Waterfront redevelopment to date and signals renewed confidence in a project that has progressed slowly since its 2020 planning approval.

The Power Station site, managed by developer Fifth Space (formerly Associate Capital), is in the midst of a multi-decade, 29-acre transformation that calls for up to 2,600 mixed-income housing units, 6.66 acres of parks and open space, retail, and a boutique hotel adapted from the historic steam power facility. The 105-unit Sophie Maxwell affordable housing building, an eight-story corten-steel structure at 1212 Maryland Street, opened in late 2025 and is now approximately 90 percent leased — one of the first tangible signs that the Power Station is becoming a functioning community.

Construction is also advancing on a UCSF Clinical and Life Sciences Building, a Herzog & de Meuron-designed seven-story cancer research center on the site's Block 2. Crews have already poured a foundation more than 65 feet below ground, according to reporting by the San Francisco Chronicle. The development agreement, approved in 2020, commits the developer to fund public infrastructure and parks on specified timelines — though the developer has requested some modifications to entitlements to help make certain phases financially feasible.

For Dogpatch neighbors, the JPMorgan investment offers a concrete sign of momentum at a site that has been a construction zone for years. The 300-foot smokestack — retained as a neighborhood landmark — remains visible across the waterfront, a marker of both the site's industrial past and its promised future.

events.title: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc at SFMOMA
events.location: SFMOMA Roberts Family Gallery, 151 Third St, SoMa
events.description: Artist Jacob Hashimoto's largest-ever installation suspends nearly 75,000 hand-built bamboo-and-paper kites from floor to ceiling in SFMOMA's free-admission Roberts Family Gallery. The immersive cloud canopy is visible through two-story windows facing Howard Street.

events.description: The 2026 Pokémon World Championships — coinciding with the franchise's 30th anniversary — takes over Moscone Center August 28–30, with more than 50,000 fans expected. The inaugural PokémonXP fan convention runs alongside, featuring cosplay competitions, panels, workshops, and a pop-up Pokémon Center store. More than 20 neighborhood businesses participate with special activations; this is the fourth-Thursday series running through September 24.

moreNews.headline: Port of San Francisco Orders Demolition Plan for Historic Pier 68–70 Drydocks
moreNews.body: The Port of San Francisco has directed global engineering firm GHD to draft a demolition plan for the Eureka Drydock (570 feet) and Drydock Number Two (900 feet) at Piers 68–70 in Dogpatch — two of the largest ship repair structures on the city's waterfront. Both drydocks were determined to be unrepairable after suffering catastrophic structural damage during severe storms last November, according to the Potrero View. Drydock Number Two, built by Bethlehem Steel Corporation in 1970, is larger than any of the Port's piers and bigger than the Ferry Building. Dogpatch Neighborhood Association member Katherine Doumani said she is concerned about potential toxic sediment leaching from DD2, though Port officials say there is currently no indication that is occurring.

moreNews.headline: Ruth Asawa Gallery Now Open at Minnesota Street Project in Dogpatch
moreNews.body: Ruth Asawa Lanier, Inc. opened a permanent gallery at Minnesota Street Project (1275 Minnesota St.) in Dogpatch in May, dedicating the 1,714-square-foot space to regular public access to Asawa's looped-wire sculptures, prints, and community projects. The gallery — the first permanent venue providing ongoing access to Asawa's work — debuted with an exhibition curated by her daughters Aiko Cuneo and Addie Lanier. The estate's decision to plant a permanent flag at the Dogpatch complex arrives as Minnesota Street Project works to refill its roster after several long-running galleries, including Rena Bransten Gallery and Altman Siegel, departed in late 2025. The current exhibition at the Ruth Asawa Lanier gallery runs August 8 through October 3, 2026.

moreNews.headline: Potrero Annex Demolition Underway After Decades of Delays
moreNews.body: Demolition of the Potrero Hill Terrace and Annex public housing complex is underway after years of repeated delays, with excavators working through 23 World War II-era buildings on Turner Terrace, Watchman Way, and Missouri Street. The teardown, managed through the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development and property manager Bell Properties, involves asbestos abatement crews, firefighter ventilation training, and excavators and is expected to take at least nine months. The demolition is the latest step in the HOPE SF program, which promised to redevelop the troubled site — subject to lethal fires, squatting, and mismanagement — into a mixed-income neighborhood. All former residents were relocated before work began.

restaurants.name: Californios
restaurants.description: Chef Val M. Cantú's two-Michelin-starred restaurant serves an inventive, California-influenced Mexican tasting menu in an intimate SoMa space, making it one of the most celebrated fine-dining destinations in the United States.

restaurants.name: Saison
restaurants.description: Chef Richard Lee's two-Michelin-starred restaurant on Townsend Street serves a seasonally driven tasting menu that marries his Chinese heritage with premium local ingredients and an open-fire kitchen.

restaurants.name: Marlowe
restaurants.description: A SoMa neighborhood staple known for its signature Marlowe Burger and classic comfort dishes with flavorful twists, served in a lively bistro setting.

restaurants.name: SOMA Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: A neighborhood go-to at Fifth and Mission offering authentic Mediterranean and Italian dishes prepared with fresh, seasonal ingredients, open for lunch through dinner daily.

restaurants.name: Montesacro Pinseria
restaurants.description: SoMa's destination for traditional Roman pinsa — an airy, crispy-crusted alternative to pizza — made with carefully sourced ingredients in a vibrant Stevenson Street setting.

restaurants.name: The Grove – Yerba Buena
restaurants.description: A warm, casual all-day spot in Yerba Buena serving breakfast, brunch, and lunch favorites in a relaxed setting popular with locals and visitors alike.

restaurants.name: Hotel Utah Saloon
restaurants.type: Historic saloon and live music bar
restaurants.description: A SoMa landmark since 1908, the Hotel Utah Saloon is a beloved dive-bar-turned-live-music-venue inside a landmarked building, recognized on San Francisco's Legacy Business Registry.

restaurants.name: Che Fico Thrive City
restaurants.description: The Mission Bay outpost of the acclaimed Che Fico brand serves housemade pastas, wood-fired dishes, and craft cocktails steps from Chase Center.

restaurants.name: ATwater Tavern
restaurants.description: A Mission Bay waterfront tavern offering American pub fare, craft beer, and panoramic bay views in a lively, sports-friendly setting near Oracle Park.
restaurants.address: Pier 48, 340 The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94107

restaurants.name: Besharam
restaurants.description: Chef Heena Patel's vibrant Dogpatch restaurant serves bold, unapologetically spiced modern Indian cuisine inspired by home cooking and Gujarat's street food culture.

restaurants.name: La Connessa
restaurants.description: A Potrero Hill gem with a striking slate-blue and gold interior, serving blistered wood-fired pizzas, housemade pastas, and California-accented Italian dishes.

restaurants.name: Mochica
restaurants.description: A beloved Potrero Hill–Dogpatch Peruvian restaurant known for creative ceviche, pisco cocktails, and vibrant flavors from Peru's diverse culinary regions.

restaurants.name: Together Lounge
restaurants.description: A cozy Dogpatch wine bar in a 1900s storefront offering an approachable selection of wines by the taste, glass, or bottle alongside daily lasagna from Marcella's Lasagneria.

restaurants.name: The Palm Court at RH San Francisco
restaurants.description: An airy, architecturally dramatic fine-dining destination inside the RH San Francisco gallery on the Potrero Hill waterfront, serving contemporary American cuisine beneath a soaring glass-and-steel atrium.
restaurants.address: 700 De Haro St, San Francisco, CA 94107

restaurants.name: Wolfsbane
restaurants.description: A Potrero Hill–Dogpatch dining destination offering a bold, seasonal California menu with a focused wine list in a refined but relaxed atmosphere.
restaurants.address: 2272 Market St (Dogpatch location — confirm before visit)

hotels.name: San Francisco Marriott Marquis
hotels.description: A 1,500-room flagship convention hotel directly connected to the Moscone Center, featuring multiple restaurants, panoramic city views, and extensive meeting facilities.

hotels.name: InterContinental San Francisco
hotels.description: A 32-story luxury hotel on Howard Street with 550 rooms, an indoor pool, and a restaurant, steps from SFMOMA and the Moscone Center.

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco Downtown SoMa
hotels.description: Formerly the Park Central Hotel, this 686-room property completed a $70-million-plus reimagining and features a large fitness studio, refreshed meeting spaces, and commissioned art from Academy of Art University graduates.

hotels.name: Canopy by Hilton San Francisco SoMa
hotels.description: A design-forward Hilton lifestyle hotel on Fourth Street in SoMa, offering locally inspired amenities, a rooftop bar, and easy access to Moscone Center and SFMOMA.

hotels.name: Hotel Zetta San Francisco
hotels.description: A creative boutique retreat in SoMa with 116 artfully appointed guestrooms, a signature S&R Lounge cocktail bar, and an arcade-style Playroom, one block from SFMOMA.

hotels.name: The Pickwick Hotel
hotels.description: A historic 1929 property in SoMa offering affordable, well-maintained rooms in a centrally located building with classic San Francisco character.

hotels.name: Hyatt Place San Francisco Downtown
hotels.description: A modern select-service hotel on Third Street in Mission Bay, convenient to Oracle Park, Chase Center, and the UCSF campus.

shops.name: Christopher's Books
shops.description: A Potrero Hill staple since 1991, housed in a gracious Victorian building on 18th Street with a handpicked selection of new titles, handwritten staff recommendations, and the feel of a neighborhood living room.

shops.name: Alexander Book Company
shops.description: A well-stocked SoMa independent offering a broad range of fiction, nonfiction, and specialty titles, popular with the downtown office crowd.

shops.name: Minnesota Street Project Shop
shops.description: The retail and publications shop at Dogpatch's Minnesota Street Project campus offers art books, prints, and editions connected to the galleries' programming.

shops.name: RH San Francisco (Restoration Hardware)
shops.description: A dramatic multi-story design gallery in Potrero Hill's converted landmark building, showcasing high-end furniture, lighting, and home décor alongside the acclaimed Palm Court restaurant.
shops.address: 700 De Haro St, San Francisco, CA 94107

shops.name: Chronicle Books
shops.description: The flagship retail outpost for San Francisco's beloved independent publisher, offering its full catalog of art, design, children's, and lifestyle books at their SoMa headquarters.

shops.name: Dandelion Chocolate
shops.description: A beloved SoMa bean-to-bar chocolate maker and café where visitors can watch chocolate being made, sample single-origin bars, and enjoy pastries in an industrial-chic setting.
shops.address: 740 Valencia St (Mission); factory at 16 Gulch, San Francisco, CA 94103

shops.name: Bolerium Books
shops.description: An appointment-based SoMa dealer specializing in rare, out-of-print, and radical books on social movements, labor history, and counterculture — a unique resource for researchers and collectors.

shops.name: Potrero Hill Nursery
shops.description: A neighborhood nursery on 17th Street offering a curated selection of plants, succulents, and garden supplies for Potrero Hill and Dogpatch residents.

shops.name: SF Mercantile at Minnesota Street Project
shops.description: A rotating retail and exhibition space within the Minnesota Street Project complex featuring housewares, gifts, and limited-edition works from Dogpatch artists-in-residence.

shops.name: Mochi at SFMOMA
shops.description: SFMOMA's acclaimed in-house design and gift shop offers a curated selection of art books, design objects, jewelry, and prints — accessible even without paid museum admission.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA)
artEntertainment.description: One of the largest modern art museums in the United States, SFMOMA anchors SoMa's cultural corridor with seven floors of rotating and permanent exhibitions, a free ground-floor gallery, and current highlight Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc.

artEntertainment.name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (YBCA)
artEntertainment.description: A multidisciplinary arts center at the heart of SoMa's Yerba Buena district presenting visual art, performance, film, and civic programming in rotating exhibitions and events.

artEntertainment.name: Minnesota Street Project
artEntertainment.description: A three-warehouse Dogpatch complex housing multiple contemporary art galleries, subsidized artist studios, and the new permanent Ruth Asawa Lanier gallery — free and open to the public.

artEntertainment.name: Museum of Craft and Design
artEntertainment.description: Located in Dogpatch's American Industrial Center, this museum presents innovative exhibitions dedicated to contemporary craft and design, bridging art and functional objects.

artEntertainment.name: SOMArts Cultural Center
artEntertainment.description: A nonprofit hub under a SoMa highway overpass showcasing politically engaged and community-driven visual art, performance, and exhibitions from diverse Bay Area artists.

artEntertainment.name: Hotel Utah Saloon
artEntertainment.description: One of San Francisco's most beloved small venues, the Hotel Utah Saloon hosts nightly live music ranging from folk and alt-country to indie rock in its storied, intimate saloon setting.

artEntertainment.name: Moscone Center
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's primary convention and events center anchoring SoMa, hosting major conferences including the 2026 Pokémon World Championships, Dreamforce, and TechCrunch Disrupt.

artEntertainment.name: Chase Center
artEntertainment.description: Home of the Golden State Warriors and one of the Bay Area's premier live entertainment venues, Chase Center hosts marquee concerts, sporting events, and major cultural events in Mission Bay.

artEntertainment.name: Oracle Park
artEntertainment.description: Home of the San Francisco Giants, Oracle Park is a celebrated ballpark on the Mission Bay waterfront that also hosts concerts, motorsports, and community events throughout the year.
artEntertainment.address: 24 Willie Mays Plaza, San Francisco, CA 94107

artEntertainment.name: Telematic Media Arts
artEntertainment.description: A SoMa gallery and creative studio space presenting exhibitions at the intersection of technology, performance, and visual art, with regular Sunday programming open to the public.

artEntertainment.name: Little Raven Gallery
artEntertainment.description: A Howard Street contemporary gallery presenting group and solo exhibitions by emerging and mid-career artists, with regular evening opening events.

gymsRecreation.name: Gene Friend Recreation Center
gymsRecreation.description: SoMa's newly rebuilt $62 million public rec center — opened August 13, 2026 — features two full-size basketball courts, a weight room, a yoga studio, multipurpose rooms, and an outdoor playground, serving children, families, and seniors.

gymsRecreation.name: Fitness SF – SoMa
gymsRecreation.description: A spacious, well-equipped SoMa gym with cardio machines, free weights, group fitness classes, and a welcoming staff popular with the neighborhood's working professionals.

gymsRecreation.name: Ritual Hot Yoga – SoMa
gymsRecreation.description: A highly rated SoMa hot yoga studio offering a large main room and a smaller red-light Yin meditation room with sound bowls, beloved by loyal members for its attentive staff and diverse class offerings.

gymsRecreation.name: Zenses Immersive Yoga Studio
gymsRecreation.type: Immersive yoga and sound healing studio
gymsRecreation.description: A SoMa sanctuary offering yoga classes, sound healing sessions, and wellness activities in a community-focused environment that blends yoga, music, art, and movement.

gymsRecreation.name: Dogpatch Boulders
gymsRecreation.description: A Touchstone Climbing gym in Dogpatch with tall walls for top-rope, lead, and bouldering routes at all skill levels, plus a weightlifting area, yoga classes, and a friendly community atmosphere.

gymsRecreation.name: Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center – UCSF Mission Bay
gymsRecreation.type: University fitness center open to public
gymsRecreation.description: UCSF's flagship Mission Bay fitness facility features three floors of equipment, an NBA basketball court, a climbing wall, dedicated Pilates studios, and a 25-yard outdoor rooftop pool voted best pool in San Francisco.

gymsRecreation.name: 3rd Street Boxing Gym
gymsRecreation.description: A no-frills, community-rooted boxing gym in Dogpatch offering training sessions and classes for all levels, with a strong local following in the Potrero Hill and Mission Bay areas.

gymsRecreation.name: Bay Padel Dogpatch
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's premier padel facility in Dogpatch, offering court rentals and lessons for the fast-growing racket sport in a modern, community-friendly space.

gymsRecreation.name: 24 Hour Fitness – Potrero Hill
gymsRecreation.description: A convenient Potrero Hill 24-hour gym offering a full range of cardio equipment, free weights, and group fitness classes for members around the clock.

gymsRecreation.name: Victoria Manalo Draves Park
gymsRecreation.description: SoMa's beloved public park named for the first Asian American Olympic gold medalist, featuring playgrounds, basketball courts, and green space — adjacent to the newly reopened Gene Friend Recreation Center.

gymsRecreation.name: Mission Bay Commons Park
gymsRecreation.description: A central green space in Mission Bay offering open lawns, a children's play area, waterfront views, and year-round programming for the neighborhood's growing population of families.

gymsRecreation.name: CrossFit Potrero Hill
gymsRecreation.description: A community-focused CrossFit box in Potrero Hill offering coached strength, conditioning, and functional fitness classes for all skill levels.
